title: Where heavy files live
question: Where should images, models, audio and screenshots live so git stops growing (about 250 MB a day now)? History and the bible are in sections 6 and 7 of the proposal; comment if you disagree.

options.label: supabase: Supabase Storage + manifest (recommended)
options.note: The plan from 2026-09-28. Files keep their paths on disk; a sync script uploads them by checksum and git keeps a manifest. Rewards in a separate bucket, encrypted before upload. About $10/month for a third active project; storage within the plan's 100 GB. Half a day to set up.

options.label: lfs: Git LFS on GitHub
options.note: Least new tooling, but LFS files in a public repo are public (no rewards), nothing can ever be deleted, and Pages serves pointer files. 10 GiB free, then about $0.07/GiB a month plus downloads.

options.label: r2: Cloudflare R2 (or Backblaze B2) + rclone
options.note: Same design as supabase for under $1/month at 50 GB, but a new account.

options.label: local-backup: local disk + encrypted nightly backup
options.note: Heavy files stay ignored on this disk; restic backs up the whole folder (rewards included, encrypted) to B2 or R2 for under $1/month. Simplest, but assets are tied to this machine and versions are by date, not by commit.

links.label: The proposal, with the measurements (a few minutes to read)

decision: Cloudflare R2 for used assets only; local machine keeps WIP and rejected; repo as lean as possible, all resources in git-ignored areas, upload what another machine needs (Jørgen, 11:44)
